To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) fear expression and return of (ROF) fear following threat instruction are enhanced by actual contingency experience, (2) fear expression and ROF following threat instruction cannot be fully overridden by safety information, and (3) ROF following reinstatment of instructed CS+s is unaffected by actual contingency experience.

CS–US contingency instructions are powerful in eliciting immediate and sustained fear reactions, but the effect of actual experience of pairings on the fear reaction is small and does not extend to the ROF following reinstament.

(1) CS-US pairings can enhance instructed fear beyond the mere effect of instructions, (2) instructions can generate immediate fear reactions that are difficult to override, and (3) instructed CS+ fear can return following reinstatement.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of contingency instructions on fear and ROF and the extent to which such effects can be modified by actual experience of CS-US pairings.
the question of whether the fear reaction to a CS can be generated by instructions alone, without actual CS–US pair experience.
the impact of instructions about a CS–US contingency, with actual CS–US experience, with fear expression and ROF, and with startle potentiation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
instructions alone can elicit conditioned responses, but the addition of actual CS–US pair experience can enhance the fear reaction.
instructions about CS–US contingencies are powerful and that actual experience of CS-US pairings can enhance the effects.
the effect of contingency instruction on fear reactions is not completely overridden by actual experience of CS-US pairings.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
contingency instructions are sufficient to generate fear reactions and ROF.
the mere instruction of a CS–US contingency is a sufficient condition to generate fear responses to the CS.
contingency instructions are a powerful tool that can generate fear responses, even without actual CS–US pair experience.
The main takeaway from our work is that
contingency instructions alone can generate fear and ROF following reinstation, but that actual experience of CS- US pairings can further enhance fear reactions.

contingency information alone can be sufficient to generate fear and that actual experience of contingencies can enhance fear reactions but does not necessarily override the effects of contingency instructions.
contingency instructions are not just a proxy for actual CS–US pairing experience.
